clue.text: Finally we can't forget Carry On with aunt's bottle exploding

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters of the aunt's bottle scatter and land in a new order

blocks.note: to last is to carry on, keep going
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A film fan's farewell list ends with a Carry On film watched while Auntie's bottle goes off with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On looks like the British comedy film series, but it is just the verb LAST, and the remaining eleven letters rearrange into BUT NOT LEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to introduce a closing item that still matters, the one remaining thing nobody should overlook.

clue.text: What has five or two more itself?

definitions.text: What has five or two more itself?

blocks.clueFragment: What has five or two more
blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle about something that holds five things, or perhaps seven
setter's reading: the word counts its own spelling, five different characters, seven in total

explanation.walkthrough: Spell the answer out: it uses five distinct characters (L, E, T, R, S), and with the repeated E and T it has two more, seven in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the symbols of an alphabet, and its own spelling has five different symbols or seven counting repeats.

clue.text: Special unit's OK intervening splitting up boozers

indicators.note: something intervening comes between, splitting up the pair so the unit sits inside OK

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for special
taken as written
a unit is one, and A means one
the apostrophe-s supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A special forces unit approves of stepping in to break up a fight among drunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaks is slang for heavy drinkers, people who soak up alcohol like sponges.

clue.text: Take a scalpel to job one: chin augmentation – it's delicate

indicators.note: cutting away most of the word with a blade leaves only its final letter behind

blocks.note: the last letter survives the surgery
taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter is the small addition grafted onto chin

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon's first operation of the day is a chin enlargement, a fiddly procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surgical vocabulary is all cover: job is trimmed to its tail, and the chin gets a one-letter implant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine translucent porcelain, prized for being thin and fragile.

clue.text: Area of water being evacuated by Portugal

indicators.note: when something is evacuated by a party, that party leaves it, so its letter goes

blocks.note: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle, a creature of the water
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A stretch of sea is cleared as the Portuguese navy pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area of water' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is the link and 'water being' is the turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a tract of land considered for its physical features, a region or stretch of ground.

clue.text: Unpopular group rocks, not all appearing for show

definitions.text: rocks, not all appearing for show

blocks.note: out of favour, no longer in
a crop can mean a batch or group, as in this year's crop of graduates

explanation.surface: A band nobody likes is playing rock, though not every member turns up for the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group rocks' sounds like a band playing music; the rocks are geological.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologically, this is bedrock that breaks the surface, so only part of the formation is exposed to view.

clue.text: Compact pads which sleepers may occupy

blocks.note: first meaning: small rounded fleshy parts, like those of the ear
second meaning: a sleeper is a small plain earring left in a pierced ear

explanation.walkthrough: Sleepers suggest people in bed or railway timbers; here they are earrings, which sit in the soft part of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlobes are small soft rounded flaps of flesh, and pierced ones are where stud earrings called sleepers are worn.

clue.text: Black resident of Martha's Vineyard maybe needs love

blocks.note: Martha's Vineyard is an island off Massachusetts, so its residents are an example of a US citizen
love is nil in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A Black islander in a Massachusetts resort is looking for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like a description of the resident, but it is the coffee order.
explanation.definitionFit: This espresso diluted with hot water is normally served without milk, as a black coffee.

clue.text: Broadcast made by space traveller supporting president

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece holds the other up, so it is written underneath

blocks.note: Donald Trump, US president
ET, the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A radio or TV programme made by an astronaut who backs the president.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim it loudly to everyone, announcing it widely as one would on air.

clue.text: One should teach about provincial painting, perhaps retrospectively

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading the whole string backwards, from its end

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
Northern Ireland is called the Province, so NI stands for provincial
painting is one example of art

explanation.surface: Someone who teaches might lecture on regional painting, reviewing it in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called simply the Province, a convention many non-British solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach or instructor trains people, so is someone whose job is to instruct others.

clue.text: Ticket for Versailles, the water spectacle

blocks.note: a tab is a bill or ticket, as in picking up the tab
in French, as spoken at Versailles, the water is l'eau

explanation.surface: A ticket to the famous fountain display in the gardens of Versailles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Versailles' tells you to translate into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or picture, often a staged group posed for show, so a visual display.

clue.text: Not bothered with run? This should suit

blocks.note: easy in the sense of relaxed, as in 'I'm easy'
to chair a meeting is to run it

explanation.surface: Someone unbothered about going for a run might prefer something more restful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: a relaxed person who would rather not run would be well suited by this seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable armchair is the natural furniture for someone laid-back who would rather sit than exercise.

clue.text: Truss, optionally reversible, used by runner to tighten belt

indicators.note: something reversible can be turned around, so her title may be read either way

blocks.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow
Liz Truss was Prime Minister, and before that a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A surgical truss with a reversible fitting is worn by a jogger who wants to cinch the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022 and long an MP, so her title works in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightening one's belt is an idiom for economising, spending as little as possible.

clue.text: Establish fact number one should be rebutted

indicators.note: a rebuttal pushes back, so the pair of words just before it is turned back to front

blocks.note: a stat, short for statistic, is a piece of factual data
NO is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Argue that an established fact, the leading point, ought to be refuted.
explanation.definitionFit: To station troops or staff is to post or settle them in a place, a verb sense of setting up.

clue.text: Member of union that's moonlighting?

blocks.note: surface reading: a trade unionist secretly working a second job
setter's reading: the union is a marriage, and the moonlighting is a secret night-time affair

explanation.walkthrough: Moonlighting usually means holding an extra job on the side; here it is taken as carrying on by moonlight outside one's marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A married person who is unfaithful to a spouse is a partner in a wedded couple seeing someone else.

clue.text: Perform piano backing with troupe's online show

indicators.note: backing here means going backwards, so the verb and the musical letter are read from the end

blocks.note: to do a play or a song is to perform it
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
the troupe's members together are the cast

explanation.surface: A pianist accompanies a theatre company in an internet performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano backing' looks like musical accompaniment, but 'backing' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is a digital audio series that listeners download or stream over the internet.

clue.text: Purge of SF incited outburst

indicators.note: an outburst is an explosion, so the letters before it are blown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A crackdown follows an angry outbreak stirred up by science fiction fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge something can mean to cleanse it of impurities, and disinfecting rids a surface of germs.

clue.text: Mumbling stuff in bed

blocks.note: first meaning: indistinct background chatter, the word actors repeat to sound like a crowd
second meaning: a plant with pink stalks grown in a garden bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff in bed' hints at whispering under the covers; the bed is a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage extras murmur this word to imitate crowd noise, and it is also a garden plant eaten in pies and crumbles.

clue.text: Food choice leads to scrap

blocks.note: choice in the sense of fine or exceptional
a scrap is a small piece

explanation.surface: Picking what to eat ends in a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap looks like a fight but is a small piece. Rarebit, Welsh rarebit, is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury dish of seasoned melted cheese on toast, so it is something eaten.

clue.text: Steal from bank over river, getting clear

blocks.note: a bar is a bank of sand or silt lying across a river mouth
to clear a sum is to net it as profit, to gain it

explanation.surface: Robbers rob a bank and flee across the river, making a clean getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The heist story hides a bargain-hunter's sense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bought very cheaply is called a steal, an item that costs far less than its worth.

clue.text: Poles acquiring company, lucky things

indicators.note: something acquiring an item takes it in, so the business abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: masts are tall poles
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Polish people buying a firm, the fortunate ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like the nationality, but its capital letter is just the opening word; these are wooden poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascots are people, animals or objects believed to bring good fortune, such as a team's charm.

clue.text: Fly-by-night getting married in the morning – first whopper!

indicators.note: first places the wedding-and-dawn pair ahead of the fly-by-night in the order of writing

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
am, ante meridiem, before noon
a moth is an insect that flies by night

explanation.surface: A shady character is getting married in the morning, a whopping first.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly-by-night is normally an untrustworthy person; here it is literally an insect flying at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is something huge, and a mammoth is an enormous thing, used as a noun for anything giant.

clue.text: Outline of Elvis Concerto's uplifting but hit-and-miss

indicators.note: hit-and-miss means taking one letter, missing the next, and so on through the words
in a down clue, lifting up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: every other letter, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A review says an Elvis Costello concert was uplifting but patchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Elvis Costello; take alternate letters of 'Elvis Concerto's' and read them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template for reproducing a shape, so it gives the outline of a design.

clue.text: One's turned or will turn 5

indicators.note: the little conjunction is turned around, its two letters swapped

blocks.note: taken as written
5-down is an outcrop, and a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop

explanation.surface: Something turns or will soon turn, a riddle about rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a hilltop of bare rock, found on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades, so it is made to spin.

clue.text: Woolly sweater unravelling at hem again …

indicators.note: unravelling here pulls the two-letter word out of the garment
woolly means fuzzy and muddled, so what remains is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A wool jumper is coming apart at the hem and needs fixing again.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AT out of SWEATER and rearrange SWEER. A sweater is a jumper, the British word for a knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: To hem a second time is to stitch it once more, since hemming is a form of sewing.

clue.text: Enjoy a retro view of bizarre Mini scenario

indicators.note: of here means taken from within the words that follow, a run of their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Fondly look back at a weird scene involving a classic Mini car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is the classic small British car, a natural object of nostalgia.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall the past fondly, taking pleasure in looking back at old times.

clue.text: … and more than half of that's wrapped in tissue

indicators.note: keeping more than half of a five-letter word means dropping its first two
the short preposition is wrapped up inside the remaining letters

blocks.note: that is the previous answer, 22-down
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the sewing story: most of the repair is wrapped in tissue paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 22-down, whose answer 'that' refers to; keep its last three letters SEW and put IN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, a band of tough fibrous body tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Person waiting in front of prison cheers when one is incarcerated

indicators.note: someone incarcerated is locked up, so the single letter is shut inside the jail

blocks.note: being behind bars means being in prison
the Roman numeral for one
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Someone queuing outside a jail celebrates as a convict is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Person waiting suggests someone in a queue; here it means someone waiting on customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee in a café, so waits on customers like a server.

clue.text: Very much at sea from cocaine?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective of vast extent

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the drug's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Is someone feeling very lost and confused because of cocaine?
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, 'very much at sea' also describes the answer literally, belonging to the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic can mean immense or vast, like an ocean, describing something huge in scale or degree.

clue.text: Give up article going into some football draw with the Spanish

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so the article goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: a throw-in is one part of a football match
the definite article
to draw a vehicle is to tow it
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sports report on a football draw against Spain, with someone quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw looks like a tied match, but it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a towel into the ring to concede the fight.
